points.notes: CONFIRMED current signature on main. Flow: ImageData* image_data = ImageData::ValidateAndCreate(...) allocates the backing NotShared<DOMUint8ClampedArray> (reachable via image_data->data()); then scoped_refptr<StaticBitmapImage> snapshot = GetImage(...); then the pixels are copied with snapshot->PaintImageForCurrentFrame().readPixels(image_data_pixmap.info(), image_data_pixmap.writable_addr(), image_data_pixmap.rowBytes(), sx, sy) where image_data_pixmap is an SkPixmap aliased over the ImageData buffer. INJECT HERE: immediately AFTER the readPixels call succeeds and BEFORE `return image_data;`, gate on base::FeatureList::IsEnabled(features::kFarbleCanvas) && a live session seed, then call PerturbPixels(image_data->data()->Data(), size_t byte_length). Mirrors Brave BraveSessionCache::PerturbPixels: walk the RGBA bytes with the per-domain mt19937_64 PRNG and flip only the low bit(s) of each channel so the change is imperceptible but deterministic per (origin, session). Do NOT perturb the StaticBitmapImage/Snapshot itself — it is shared with compositing/drawImage and would corrupt on-screen rendering. Perturb only at each JS-facing readback exit. Note buffer may be RGBA or BGRA depending on color space / kN32; perturb per-channel-agnostically.

points.realFunction: std::unique_ptr<webrtc::PortAllocator> PeerConnectionDependencyFactory::CreatePortAllocator(blink::WebLocalFrame* web_frame)  (moved from content/renderer into Blink modules/peerconnection in ~M92+; this is the current path).
points.notes: CONFIRMED on main. This is the PREFERRED, non-hacky suppression point — no string filtering of candidates. It calls Platform::Current()->GetWebRTCRendererPreferences(web_frame, &webrtc_ip_handling_policy, &min_port, &max_port, &allow_mdns_obfuscation); then a switch on the policy sets a P2PPortAllocator::Config port_config with: enable_multiple_routes, enable_nonproxied_udp, enable_default_local_candidate. Mapping: kDefault -> multiple_routes=true,nonproxied_udp=true (leaks LAN + public); kDefaultPublicAndPrivateInterfaces / kDefaultPublicInterfaceOnly -> multiple_routes=false; kDisableNonProxiedUdp -> multiple_routes=false AND nonproxied_udp=false. When enable_multiple_routes is true it wraps network_manager in FilteringNetworkManager(network_manager_.get(), media_permission, allow_mdns_obfuscation); the allocator is std::make_unique<P2PPortAllocator>(std::move(network_manager), socket_factory_, port_config, ...). To be coherent with a proxy exit and leak nothing: force policy == kDisableNonProxiedUdp so multiple_routes=false + nonproxied_udp=false -> host/srflx UDP suppressed, only proxied TCP/TLS TURN candidates form, giving the proxy's IP only. Under the hood these config bools translate to cricket/webrtc PORTALLOCATOR_DISABLE_UDP | PORTALLOCATOR_DISABLE_STUN | PORTALLOCATOR_DISABLE_ADAPTER_ENUMERATION | PORTALLOCATOR_DISABLE_DEFAULT_LOCAL_CANDIDATE (defined in third_party/webrtc/p2p/base/port_allocator.h) applied via PortAllocator::set_flags(). You may also directly OR those flags after allocator creation, but driving it through the IP-handling policy is the maintainable path. mDNS: FilteringNetworkManager + MdnsResponderAdapter (mdns_responder = std::make_unique<MdnsResponderAdapter>(...)) replaces private IPs with .local hashes; with nonproxied_udp disabled you suppress even those.

points.notes: This is where you inject the per-profile choice WITHOUT patching WebRTC internals. flagPlumbing: Declare a base::Feature and gate every hook on it so it is runtime-togglable via --enable-features=/--disable-features= and A/B-able. For Blink-consumable features put it in third_party/blink/common/features.cc with the declaration in third_party/blink/public/common/features.h: `BASE_FEATURE(kFarbleCanvas, \"FarbleCanvas\", base::FEATURE_DISABLED_BY_DEFAULT);` (repeat kFarbleWebRTC, kSpoofNavigator). Gate at each injection site with `if (base::FeatureList::IsEnabled(blink::features::kFarbleCanvas)) { ... }`. Cross-process correctness is automatic: the browser process's FeatureList state is serialized onto the renderer command line (the field-trial/--enable-features handoff) during renderer launch, so IsEnabled() returns the same answer in the renderer where these Blink hooks run — no extra IPC needed. For finer per-origin/JS-visible gating you could additionally add a flag in third_party/blink/renderer/platform/runtime_enabled_features.json5 (queried via RuntimeEnabledFeatures::FarbleCanvasEnabled()), but that is compile/origin-trial-oriented; the base::Feature is the right runtime kill-switch. Combine the feature check AND a non-empty session seed (feature on but seed absent = no-op) so an unconfigured profile never perturbs. Register the features in the about://flags list (chrome/browser/about_flags.cc) if you want user-facing toggles.
seedPlumbing: Mirror Brave's BraveSessionCache (brave/third_party/blink/renderer/brave_session_cache.{h,cc}), which is a Supplement<ExecutionContext> — one instance per Document AND per worker/worklet global scope, retrieved by BraveSessionCache::From(ExecutionContext&). Two ingredients: (1) a per-session/per-profile random token created ONCE in the browser process (Brave: a global uint64 g_session_token in BraveContentBrowserClient) and (2) the ExecutionContext's top-frame registrable domain (eTLD+1). The token reaches every renderer as a command-line switch appended in ContentBrowserClient::AppendExtraCommandLineSwitches (Brave switch: kBraveSessionToken); the renderer reads it once via base::CommandLine::ForCurrentProcess()->GetSwitchValueASCII(...) into a process global. In the supplement, domain_key_ = HMAC/hash(domain, session_token); FarblingPRNG() returns a std::mt19937_64 seeded from domain_key_, and PerturbPixels(unsigned char* data, size_t size) walks the RGBA buffer using that PRNG to flip low bits — deterministic per (origin, session), stable across getImageData/toDataURL/toBlob within a page, different across origins and across sessions. To adapt for your per-profile antidetect browser: since each profile launches its own renderer process, append a per-profile token switch (e.g. --myapp-session-token=<uint64> plus the per-profile UA/platform/hw-concurrency config) in your ContentBrowserClient (or, in Electron, deliver via blink::RendererPreferences which is already per-session and avoids a fork). Create the Supplement<ExecutionContext> exactly like BraveSessionCache::From, seed the PRNG from hash(topframe_etld1, token), and expose GetPRNG()/PerturbPixels() to the canvas hooks and (optionally) hardwareConcurrency. Because it hangs off ExecutionContext it is reachable from both frame and worker Navigator/canvas code and each thread gets its own supplement instance, keeping it thread-safe without shared mutable state.
